probes.question: What does the Panjikent archive suggest about paper?
options: It was already known in Central Asia before 751
It was only used by Chinese emperors

probes.question: True or false: the oldest known fragments of the precursor of modern paper date to the 2nd century BCE in China.

image.alt: A Chinese woodcut-style illustration of a papermaker dipping a screen into a brick vat of paper pulp
image.credit: Collection of reproductions of Ming dynasty woodcuts / Wikimedia Commons

body.claim: Paper probably reached Central Asia before the famous Battle of Talas.
body.why: Popular history says papermaking spread west after the Battle of Talas in 751 CE, when captured Tang papermakers revealed their secrets. But an archive of 76 paper writings in Sogdian, Arabic and Chinese was found at Panjikent, left by its ruler before the city was captured by Arabs in 722. Paper itself is much older: the pulp process is ascribed to Cai Lun in the 2nd century CE, and the oldest known fragments of its precursor date to the 2nd century BCE in China.
